cards.text: The prophet Ezekiel (Ezekiel 1:3) says the word of the LORD came to him. God calls him 'Son of man' and tells him to pose a riddle and speak a parable to the house of Israel. I LOVE a good riddle, friend, and this one comes from the LORD Himself.
Here's the riddle: a great eagle with great wings, long pinions and feathers of many colors comes to Lebanon. That eagle didn't fly in, friend, he made an ENTRANCE.

cards.question: What does this great eagle take in Lebanon?

cards.text: The eagle plucks off the cedar's topmost shoot, carries it to the land of merchants and plants it in a city of traders. Then he takes some of the seed of the land and plants that too, like a gardener who actually read the back of the packet.

cards.question: The eagle plants the seed of the land by abundant waters, in ___ soil.
The seed the eagle planted grows into a tall tree that towers over everything around it.

cards.text: It sprouts into a spreading vine, low in height, with its roots staying right where it stood. Low but spreading, friend, which is also how I'd describe my mustache.

cards.question: Which way do this low vine's branches turn?

answers.text: Toward the eagle who planted it

cards.text: But hold on, there's ANOTHER great eagle with great wings and many feathers. Two great eagles and one low vine, and I'm nervous already.

cards.question: When the second great eagle shows up, the vine bends its roots toward him.
The vine stretches out its branches to the second eagle so that he might ___ it.

cards.text: And here's the wild part: that vine was ALREADY planted in good soil by abundant waters, set up to bear fruit and become a splendid vine. That's sitting at your desk, on the company laptop, emailing your resume to the competition.
Then God asks, 'Will it flourish?' Friend, I'm leaning in so far my gold base is tipping.

cards.question: What does God say will happen to this vine that reached for the second eagle?

answers.text: It will be uprooted and wither
It will grow into a cedar
It will bear a great harvest

cards.question: God says it will take a strong arm and many people to pull this vine up by its roots.

cards.text: Then God asks again: even if it's transplanted, will it flourish? A fresh start somewhere new, friend. Let's see.

cards.question: Even if the vine is transplanted, God says something will strike it and make it completely wither. What is it?

cards.text: God says it will wither right on the bed where it sprouted. That's packing for a big road trip, and the car dies in your own DRIVEWAY.
The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel again, and God tells him to ask this rebellious house, 'Do you not know what these things mean?' Then God explains it, and friend, I am SO relieved.

cards.question: In God's explanation, who comes to Jerusalem and carries off its king and officials?

cards.text: So that flashy first eagle is the king of Babylon, and the topmost shoot is Jerusalem's king and officials, carried off to Babylon. I KNEW those feathers were royalty.

cards.question: Then the king of Babylon takes a member of Jerusalem's royal family. What does he do with him?

answers.text: Makes a covenant with him under oath
Makes him a servant in his palace
Puts him in chains in the city

cards.text: So that member of the royal family is the seed the eagle planted. Then the king of Babylon carries away the leading men of the land.

cards.question: The king of Babylon carries off the leading men so the kingdom will be strong enough to stand on its own.

cards.text: So the kingdom is brought low, surviving only by keeping that covenant. But that member of the royal family is king now, and he rebels against Babylon.

cards.question: Where does this king send his envoys when he rebels against Babylon?
What does this king who rebelled against Babylon ask Egypt for?

cards.text: Then God asks, 'Can he break a covenant and yet escape?' And God answers it Himself: as surely as He lives, this king isn't getting away with it.

cards.question: God says the king who broke the covenant will die in Babylon, in the land of the king who enthroned him.
God says Pharaoh, king of Egypt, with his mighty army and vast horde, will help the king who broke the covenant in battle.

cards.text: God says this king gave his hand in pledge yet did all these things, and he will not escape. He gave his HAND on it, friend. His HAND!
Then God says He'll bring down on this king's head 'My oath that he despised and My covenant that he broke.' God calls that oath and that covenant His OWN, friend.

cards.question: God says, 'I will spread My ___ over him and catch him in My snare.'

cards.text: God says He'll bring him to Babylon and judge him there for the treason he committed against God Himself.

cards.question: The choice troops of the king who broke the covenant fall by the sword. What happens to the ones who survive?

answers.text: They are scattered to every wind
They are hidden in the hills
They are sent home to Jerusalem

cards.text: Then God says, 'Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken.' But don't close the cookie box yet, friend.

cards.question: Back in the riddle, an eagle took the top of the cedar. This time, who takes a shoot from the lofty top of the cedar?

cards.text: The LORD says He will pluck a tender sprig from its topmost shoots and set it out. Not an eagle this time, friend.

cards.question: Where does the LORD say He will plant this tender sprig?

answers.text: On the mountain heights of Israel

cards.question: God says the tender sprig will bear branches, yield fruit and become a majestic ___.
God says only eagles will nest under this majestic cedar.

cards.text: Then God says all the trees of the field will know that He is the LORD, and He says, 'I bring the tall tree down.'

cards.question: Right after bringing the tall tree down, what does God say He does with the low tree?
God says He dries up the green tree.

cards.text: God says He makes the withered tree flourish, and then, 'I, the LORD, have spoken, and I have done it.' Take it from a worn-out stamper who spent years in the back of a junk drawer, friend: I LOVE that line.
